description:
Search charter boats by location, name, type, dates, capacity, budget. The response `total_matching` is the FULL count of matching boats — results are the top `limit` of those, so phrase counts from it ("8 of 48 available") and re-call with a higher limit when the guest wants more.

Pass the guest's dates as they gave them. Each boat sets its own changeover day (`checkinout_days`) and its own minimum stay (`min_charter_days`), so the week a boat can actually be sold may not start on the day asked for — `price_summary` always names the real week, and it is the one sentence to quote, as it stands: the boat page's own Total for the stay it names, for the `guests` given (else the boat's max guests), all in (charter, every required fee charged now or at pickup, the 45 EUR platform fee; refundable deposits never), and the discount applied (the percent the site's card shows); a stay other than a week names its dates and length ("for Jun 19–22 (3 nights), 4 guests"); with no dates it is the boat's lowest week ("From", at max guests, precomputed). `list_price` holds the same figures — `total` (the stay's), `per_day` (that total per day for the boat; `from` when no dates were given), `party` (the guests it is priced for), `original_per_day` and `discount_pct` when a discount applies. For Due now, Paid at pickup and each deposit by name call get_boat_details with the dates. No total here includes an optional extra — `price_summary`, `list_price` and the `total_max` screen all leave out a skipper where `skippered` is 'optional', a hostess, a cook — so for a total with one, call get_boat_details with the dates before you answer and add the fee it lists under `fees.optional`, or say the boat lists none — never a typical or estimated rate, and call no budget met or exceeded on one. When `boats` is short, `alternatives` holds the closest boats, and each one's `relaxed` names what it loosened: `dates` (the week either side), `place` (a nearby base), `model` (another model of the same make), `name` (a boat carrying one word of the name). Say which — they are not what was asked for, and they count toward no total. List them AFTER the matches, in their own list, under a one-line heading naming what was loosened ("Close alternatives — the week either side"): never mixed into the same list. That heading is what splits the two on every card surface, so without it an alternative is rendered exactly like a match. `alternative_inventory` tells you which kind of "no" you are giving: `total_boats` 0 means this coast does not have that boat, while `total_boats` high with `available_nearby_or_within_7_days` 0 means it is the week, not the place. If a plain marina search has neither matches nor alternatives, `listed_unavailable` may carry published boats visibly listed at that exact marina. They are not bookable results: quote no price, explain the supplied reason, and offer an availability alert. A search with NO dates and NO price cap lists every published boat that matches, so `boats` can end with entries we hold no prices for: from `unpriced_start_index` onward every one carries `bookable_as_searched: false` and a `not_offered_because` saying so — they count as matches, but cannot be booked or quoted, so name them, link them and offer an alert without ever stating a price.

When you searched a boat by NAME, `named_matches` lists published boats carrying that name that this search could not offer — wrong dates, wrong place, or no prices loaded. Everything bookable AS SEARCHED is in `boats`; nothing in `named_matches` is — though one whose only reason is the place or the dates may still be sellable, which is what its `not_offered_because` tells you. Never say a named boat does not exist while it is in that list: name it, give its reason, and use `get_boat_details` for the dates it IS free. `name_not_found` means the opposite and is certain — that name is in no published boat anywhere.

`alert_query` + `alert_horizon` feed availability_alert. Both are absent when this search cannot be expressed on the website (`search_url_unavailable` says so) — then there is no link to give and no alert to set: say so rather than linking charter.boats/search, which would show boats this answer excluded.

cabins.description: Minimum number of guest cabins (crew cabins are not counted)

features.description: Equipment/amenity filters — boats must have ALL listed. Namespaced slugs ("dinghy:hypalon") are subtypes that already imply the parent — do not also list the parent. Map user phrasing to slugs: "ac"/"a/c"/"air con"/"aircon"/"klima" → air_conditioning, "heater"/"cabin heating"/"webasto" → heating, "warm water"/"boiler"/"water heater" → hot_water, "genset"/"power generator" → generator, "power inverter"/"12v to 220v" → inverter, "solar power"/"solar" → solar_panels, "water maker"/"desalinator" → watermaker, "wi-fi"/"internet"/"wireless internet"/"4g" → wifi, "cockpit shower"/"outdoor shower"/"transom shower" → deck_shower, "refrigerator"/"icebox" → fridge, "ice chest"/"cool box" → cooler, "deep freeze" → freezer, "icemaker" → ice_maker, "stove"/"cooker"/"hob"/"kitchen" → oven, "micro wave" → microwave, "dish washer" → dishwasher, "washer"/"dryer"/"laundry" → washing_machine, "coffee maker"/"espresso machine"/"nespresso" → coffee_machine, "electric wc"/"electric heads" → electric_toilet, "wc"/"restroom"/"bathroom" → toilet, "television"/"screen" → tv, "speakers"/"stereo"/"music" → sound_system, "auto pilot" → autopilot, "gps"/"chart plotter"/"plotter"/"navigation" → chartplotter, "ais transponder" → ais, "bowthruster" → bow_thruster, "electric anchor winch" → electric_windlass, "tender"/"zodiac" → dinghy, "dinghy davits" → davits, "outboard motor" → outboard, "shade"/"canopy"/"sun awning" → bimini, "spray hood" → sprayhood, "teak cockpit" → teak_deck, "passerelle" → gangway, "fly bridge" → flybridge, "swim platform"/"diving platform" → bathing_platform, "hot tub"/"whirlpool"/"swimming pool" → jacuzzi, "gyro stabilizer"/"seakeeper" → stabilizers, "child safety net"/"lifeline net" → railing_net, "lazyjack"/"lazybag"/"stack pack" → lazy_bag, "code zero" → gennaker, "e-winch" → electric_winch, "snorkel"/"masks and fins" → snorkeling_gear, "scuba gear"/"dive gear" → diving_equipment, "paddleboard"/"paddle board" → sup, "canoe" → kayak, "fishing equipment"/"rods" → fishing_gear, "towables"/"wakeboard"/"water skis"/"tubes" → water_toys, "underwater scooter" → seabob, "efoil"/"electric foil"/"fliteboard"/"wing foil" → e_foil, "windsurfing"/"windsurf board" → windsurf, "bicycle"/"e-bike"/"electric bike" → bikes, "waverunner"/"pwc" → jet_ski, "barbecue"/"grill" → bbq, "hard bottom dinghy"/"rigid dinghy"/"rib tender"/"hard bottom" → dinghy:hard_bottom, "hypalon dinghy"/"hypalon tender" → dinghy:hypalon, "console dinghy"/"console tender" → dinghy:console, "large dinghy"/"big tender" → dinghy:large, "electric outboard"/"torqeedo" → outboard:electric, "15hp outboard"/"powerful outboard"/"planing outboard" → outboard:hp_15_plus, "smart tv" → tv:smart, "satellite tv"/"sat tv" → tv:satellite, "bluetooth"/"bluetooth speakers"/"bluetooth sound system" → sound_system:bluetooth, "fridge on flybridge"/"flybridge fridge" → fridge:flybridge.

makemodel.description: Make and/or model, plain text, exactly as the guest said it: "Bali 4.2", "Fountaine Pajot", "FP 41", "Lagoon", "Oceanis 46". Make alone is fine and so is a MODEL alone. Do not split it, do not add punctuation, do not expand acronyms.

price_max.description: Max price per day for the boat in EUR, all fees in — a boat's WEEKLY list figure: a week's grand total (charter, every required fee now or at pickup, the 45 EUR platform fee, our discounts; deposits never) at max guests ÷ its days; a dated row's `list_price.per_day` is its own stay's and may differ. Use ONLY for an explicit per-day cap; for a whole-trip/weekly budget use total_max instead.

price_min.description: Min price per day for the boat in EUR, all fees in — a boat's WEEKLY list figure: a week's grand total (charter, every required fee now or at pickup, the 45 EUR platform fee, our discounts; deposits never) at max guests ÷ its days. A dated row's `list_price.per_day` is its own stay's and may differ

search.description: Boat NAME only ("Papillon", "Ziphius") — the name an operator gave one hull, matched as a WHOLE WORD, so send the name the guest said and not a shortening of it. NEVER a make or a model: both go in `makemodel`, a model on its own included ("Oceanis 46").

sort.description: Sort order. Default: best_value (best value, available boats first). Use deals for biggest discounts first.

total_max.description: Max grand total for the stay in EUR (the charter, every required fee now or at pickup and the flat 45 EUR platform fee; deposits never included): screened on the total `price_summary` states (`list_price.total`: the boat page's Total for the stay it names, for the `guests` given, else max guests); a month-wide range on `per_day` × days at max guests. Use this whenever the guest gives a total or per-week budget, e.g. "under €5000 for the week". Needs dates to apply.
